I was gonna make this suggestion in response to someone else but the voat crapped out on me and kept saying I must wait 30 second to post. Fortunately I had the post saved and I might as well give you my idea since you're willing to work to get Voat in the right place.

What I'm suggesting is a multi-stage voting system - to prevent possible brigading and hijacking while properly functioning as a working voting process to make the necessary changes to a community when there is a general consensus and desire for it.

So the basic gist of it is this:

For first stage, there's no real voting process. Each subs have by default "Initiate voting process" button on the sidebar with a meter underneath to show the progress. The meter keeps the progress of the button presses by sub's users within a timeframe (a week or a month), and when there's enough users that initiated the process (for example, 51% of the subverse's monthly unique users), the stage progresses to the next one.

During the second stage, an automated sticky goes on top of the subverse, with a title "Sticky: the voting process has been initiated. Make your response to discuss on it" Or something in that line. There, users will be able to discuss on why the process has been initiated and what to do with it. Each individual users will be able to post their own preprogrammed event trigger (from a select list of options), with a lengthy explanation rationalizing it and trying to convince other users. And other users can respond to those comment threads for further discussions. Whoever gets the most upvotes for their trigger that becomes the third stage. If there's not enough votes to pass the community minimum, the process will cease and the post archived for future references.

The event trigger will read like "Replace mod XX with YY" or "change community rules" with the said explanation that follows it as written originally by the user who put it up.

Third stage will be the actual voting process. Once the event trigger is chosen by community consensus and vote, the event will by system be put to the vote for the whole community. Once the vote passes, the system automatically fulfills the event and does what the community voted it to do.

Also to prevent possible vote rigging I suggest vote weight by position and contribution. For example (from my previous post):

Admins get 5% vote weight flat each, mod of the subverse in question minus the person being replaced 1%, users of the subverse divide among them 50% share and the rest are to all Voat users.

And the subverse user share further divides by user contributions. Top 5% contributing users get 10%, top 20, 20%, and the rest get 30%.

Obviously I'm quickly just pulling out numbers so it'd have to be balanced - because if there's more than 20 admins they obviously can't have 5% each, but vote weight by positions and contributions could do well enough to counteract the abuse, but it should be enough to replace if there's a mismanagement.

All in all the ratio would be around 60% users vs 40% admin/mods so if the community is truly in unison the vote will go through.

It may not be the most ideal as you say, but we all know mailing admins and pleading them to solve anything does not work if SJW infiltrates the admin ranks. The solution has to be mechanical by design.

For the reference, first and the second stage would be entirely voted by users, and only the third stage would have admin/mod vote input.

I think you can put my idea to better use than I can.

And further, if the process fails, there would be cooldown periods corresponding to each of the stages.

i.e. 1 week CD if it fails on the first stage, 1 month if it fails on the second, and 3 months on the third stage, etc.
